commits.message:
Review: one OKLab conversion, the gallery test samples mid-phase near a million (rich-animation-42lg.6wt)

- labOf is the one polar-to-OKLab spelling; deltaE and toRgba both use it.
- The every-kind test asserts it is at 1 fps, and seeks half a second
  after a frame so the draws near 10^6 s fall mid-phase, not on whole seconds.
- kinds.ts: effected takes no identity-function mode; the border kinds use
  aroundPanel, which names the panel once.

The every-kind playground test draws at the times it checks (rich-animation-42lg.6wt)

The test was named for three draws and made about 1,900: 32 seconds of
clock at sixty frames a second, each frame the whole 120x90 gallery.
It now plays at the playground's one-frame-a-second rate, so the half
minute is a frame a second. Locally 11.3 s -> 0.27 s; it timed out at
30 s on CI.

Two costs in the frame itself, found on the way:

- kinds.ts made every effect anew inside draw(t), so a gradient's
  legible-ink memo started cold on every frame. Each effect is now made
  once and drawn with frameAt.
- Oklch.deltaE worked out four sines and cosines per comparison; a
  colour matched against a 256-colour palette paid them per entry. Each
  colour now keeps its OKLab a and b, by the same formula.

Gallery draw at 256 colours: 3.7 -> 2.6 ms, flat from t = 0 to 10^6.

Animations and effects are placed like any renderable (rich-animation-27tq.50o) (#501)

* Animations and effects are placed like any renderable (rich-animation-27tq.50o)

An Animation of renderables is a renderable: placed in any container — a
Panel, a Table cell, a Group, a container written outside rich-js — it
draws at the frame's time (RenderOptions.frame; 0 when printed) and stamps
its cells with its hold. The type carries the face exactly when the values
are renderables, so Animation<number> is refused where a renderable goes.

- core/animation: Timed<T> (the old interface) and the conditional
  Animation<T>; Animation.of attaches the face (NoInfer on its return, so
  an annotated `const a: Animation<Renderable> = Animation.of({...})`
  infers from the literal). shownAt, stamp/stampFrame and the face
  (placedRender/Measure/Contents, drawnAt) live here; tier 5.
- A stamp is the whole hold: Style.lastChange beside nextChange, layered
  as an intersection; Segment.lastChange reads it. Every stamper stamps
  both ends (face, Effected/GlyphEffected, Spinner, textFrameAt, the
  TextInput caret, ScrollFrame's carrier, frameAt).
- Effected/GlyphEffected take no t: they are the animations, at(t) the
  Recolored/Reglyphed value, with their exact face. Spinner and
  FrameSequence are placed too.
- Hosts: every view is on the timeline; HostView loses "animation",
  FrameSays loses `silent` (every view is), held is a paused timeline.
  A Live polls every view at its rate; a reduced view is no longer held.
- Frame-clock rule: a placed animation inside another's value draws at
  the frame's time (docs/animation.md, "Placing one").

test/renderables/placed.test.ts is the epic's proof: a user-declared Box
container holding a tween and an Effected gradient, drawn by an App, with
Panel/Table/Columns/Layout/Group giving the same wakes.

* Review fixes: frameAt is placement at a named time; a cell's hold is whole (rich-animation-27tq.50o)

- frameAt's renderable draws the animation placed in a frame drawn for t,
  so an Effected stamps its exact hold (a no-colour Progress pulse sleeps
  again) and animations inside its value draw at t. drawnAt folded into
  placedRender.
- Animation.of copies every member, own and inherited, as own properties
  (membersOf): a class instance keeps its methods, and a spread is whole.
- Style carries one `hold` (both ends) instead of two optional fields: a
  cell saying only nextChange claimed it always was, and a reversed
  timeline never woke for it.
- Timed and Hold exported from the main barrel.
